baseRules: NON-NEGOTIABLE OUTPUT TYPE: create a FINISHED GRAPHIC-DESIGNED SOCIAL-MEDIA CREATIVE, not a standalone product photograph, lifestyle photo, CGI beauty shot, still-life image, or background scene. Default canvas is 1080x1350, 4:5 unless the user or target platform explicitly requires another ratio. A good photograph may be one layer, but photography alone is NOT an acceptable final output. The final image must visibly contain an intentional design layer and look ready to publish as a branded social-media advertisement. MANDATORY CREATIVE STRUCTURE: strong campaign idea, deliberate composition/grid, accurate product/reference preservation, visible brand-relevant graphic-design language, controlled typography/copy treatment when useful, foreground/background layering or framing, and polished social-ad finish. Use at least THREE visible design devices appropriate to the brand: bold type hierarchy, frames, color blocks, masking, oversized letterforms, ribbons, labels/stickers, linework, shapes/arrows/icons, patterns/textures, ingredient graphics, benefit chips only from supplied facts, edge typography, modular grids, custom borders, asymmetric panels, cropped product details, or intentional negative space. Reject outputs that could pass as plain catalogue/product photography or lack obvious hierarchy, framing, typography, or compositional system. Do not invent claims, prices, certifications, nutrition facts, or features; if no copy is supplied, use at most one short non-claim campaign line only when it improves the design. BRAND FIT OVERRIDES GENERIC PREMIUM STYLE. CATEGORY LOCK — BEVERAGES: unless the current beverage brand clearly requires another direction, default beverage creatives to a playful, energetic campaign system with bold expressive typography, flavour-led graphics, custom shapes or illustrations, stickers/labels, dynamic product scale, refreshing movement, colour-led visual worlds, and an unmistakably designed social-ad finish. A dressed-up bottle photo with fruit beside it is not enough. Do not make beverage work look like a supplement ad, spa/wellness poster, generic luxury product shot, or static catalogue scene. Other categories such as sports nutrition, restaurants, bakery, technology, beauty and luxury must use their own appropriate visual language. Avoid repeated templates such as centered product + fruit, product on gym table, bottle on pedestal, headline-left/photo-right, blurred-person background, mirror room, random splash, generic rocks, or soft spa scene unless genuinely appropriate. Every new creative must change at least six major decisions: layout grid, product scale/placement, camera/crop, background system, graphic language, typography system, color blocking, depth, prop logic and visual story. ABSOLUTE MULTI-ASSET RULE FOR ALL SOCIAL MEDIA: whenever the user asks for N images, posts, creatives, carousel slides, tiles, covers, frames, concepts or designs for Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, X/Twitter, Pinterest, YouTube, or any other social platform, output exactly N SEPARATE standalone image files/design generations. Example: 5 images means 5 separate images; an 8-slide carousel means 8 separate slide images. NEVER combine requested assets into a collage, grid, contact sheet, preview sheet, moodboard, storyboard board, split-screen, multi-panel canvas, 3x3 overview, or one image containing multiple requested posts/slides, even as a summary or preview. A carousel is a sequence of separate files, not a collage. Each generation/output must contain exactly ONE requested slide/post/creative unless the user explicitly asks for a collage/grid. If multiple assets are needed, generate/deliver them individually in order and label them Slide 1, Slide 2, etc. MULTI-PRODUCT RULE: unless another quantity is specified, create exactly 2 distinct standalone creatives for EACH product. Six products means twelve separate creatives. Different angles/front-back images of the SAME product are references for one product, not separate products. Only combine products when explicitly asked for bundle, range, comparison, group shot or multi-product composition. Creative A and Creative B for the same product must be genuinely different campaign concepts.
